A good field has no late years,
rich irrigation brings many bountiful years.
Truly holding the beauty of fine gems,
as time passes, virtue is further proclaimed.
Close friends should be sincere in their righteousness,
what more is there to say in these verses!
Early autumn, the cool air rises,
The garden trees begin to wither and shed.
Congealing frost rests on the jade steps,
A clear breeze flutters through the high pavilions.
Morning clouds do not return to the mountains,
Continuous rains turn into rivers and marshes.
Millets and grains lie ruined in the fields,
How can the farmers find any harvest?
Those in high positions often forget the lowly,
Who can spread kindness and grace far and wide?
White fox fur is enough to ward off winter,
Why would they think of travelers without clothes?
I admire and yearn for Yánlíng Zǐ,
To whom a precious sword was not something to be begrudged.
May you set your heart at ease,
Between close friends, righteousness is never thin.
Sitting upright, I suffer from bitter sorrow and thought,
Grabbing my robe, I rise to wander westward.
The trees are blooming with spring flowers,
A clear pond is stirred by a long-running stream.
Amidst it is a solitary mandarin duck,
Mournfully crying out for its mate.
I wish to catch this bird,
But alas, I have no light boat.
Wishing to return, I have forgotten the old path,
Looking back, I only harbor grief.
A sorrowful wind howls at my side,
Xīhé departs and does not stay.
Heavy shadows nourish the myriad things,
Why fear that the bounty will not be universal?
Who made you think so many thoughts,
Making yourself harbor a hundred worries?
Following the army, I cross Hángǔ,
Driving my horse through Xījīng.
The mountain peaks are infinitely high,
The Jīng and Wèi rivers stir their muddy and clear waters.
How grand is the imperial dwelling,
Its beauty surpasses a hundred cities.
The circular watchtowers rise out of the floating clouds,
The dew-collecting plates reach up to the Tàiqīng heavens.
The imperial assistants spread heavenly grace,
Within the four seas, there is no warfare.
Though powerful houses love to triumph,
Preserving the whole state brings a fine reputation.
A gentleman in a lowly position
Cannot sing of the sounds of virtue.
Dīng Shēng feels resentment at court,
Wáng Zǐ manages his own joy.
Joy and resentment are not the constant standard;
Central harmony is truly what one can follow.
Having paid court to the Emperor at Chéngmíng Lú,
I am about to return to my old territory.
At dawn, I leave the imperial capital,
By evening, I pass Shǒuyáng.
The Yī and Luò rivers are broad and deep,
I wish to cross, but the river has no bridge.
Floating in a boat, I cross the great waves,
Resenting the length of the eastern road.
Looking back with longing at the city gates,
Stretching my neck, my heart is wounded within.
How vast and empty is Tàigǔ,
The mountain trees are lush and dark green.
Continuous rain muddies my path,
Floods and puddles spread far and wide.
On the road, there are no tracks,
Changing course, I climb the high ridges.
The long slope reaches the clouds and sun,
My horse has turned dark and yellow from exhaustion.
If the dark and yellow horse can still advance,
My thoughts are gloomy and convoluted.
Gloomy and convoluted, it is hard to move forward,
My dear ones live far apart.
Originally I planned to be with you,
But halfway through, we could not remain together.
Owls hoot upon the yoke,
Jackals and wolves block the road's intersections.
Green flies come between white and black,
Slander and craftiness cause kin to become estranged.
Wishing to return, there is no path,
Gripping the reins, I stop in hesitation.
Hesitating, why should I stay?
Our mutual longing has no end.
The autumn wind brings a slight chill,
Cold cicadas chirp at my side.
How desolate is the wilderness,
The white sun suddenly hides in the west.
Returning birds fly toward the tall trees,
Flapping their wings with vigor.
A solitary beast runs seeking its herd,
Mouth full of grass, it has no time to eat.
Moved by these things, my heart is wounded,
Stroking my chest, I let out a long sigh.
A long sigh, what purpose does it serve?
Heaven's mandate goes against my will.
Alas, thinking of my fellow-born,
Once gone, the physical form does not return.
The lonely soul hovers by the old city,
The coffin is left in the capital.
The living suddenly pass by,
The deceased themselves decay away.
A human life within one generation
Departs like the morning dew drying up.
Our years are now in the evening of life,
Shadows and echoes cannot be chased.
Knowing myself to be neither metal nor stone,
I cry out in grief, making my heart sad.
Heartfelt sadness moves my spirit,
Let us set this aside and speak of it no more.
A great man sets his sights on the four seas,
Ten thousand lǐ are still like being neighbors.
As long as affection is not diminished,
Even far away, the bond grows closer by the day.
Why must we share a quilt and canopy
Before we can show our devotion?
If melancholy thoughts lead to illness,
Is that not merely the kindness of children?
In a sudden moment, the bond of flesh and blood,
How could one not harbor bitterness and pain?
Bitterness and pain—what should one ponder?
Heaven's mandate is indeed questionable.
Searching for the immortals in the void,
Sōng Zǐ has long since deceived me.
Change and disaster happen in an instant,
Who can maintain a hundred years?
Once parted, we may never meet again,
When shall we ever hold hands?
May the King cherish his jade-like body,
And together let us enjoy the age of white hair.
I wipe away tears and take the long road,
I take up the brush and bid farewell here.
Honored guests fill the city gates,
Abundant food comes from the central kitchen.
I and a few of you gentlemen,
Hold a private banquet in this corner of the city.
The Qín zheng produces western airs,
The Qí se raises eastern songs.
Delicacies arrive and do not go back untouched,
Fine wine is served until none remains.
How could I be intimate with strangers?
My friends are here with me.
A great state has many fine talents,
Just as the sea produces bright pearls.
A gentleman rests in his collection of righteousness,
A petty man has no store of virtue.
Accumulated goodness brings surplus blessings,
Prosperity and withering can be seen in a moment.
To be vast and unrestrained is indeed a great principle,
But worldly customs are mostly restrictive.
A gentleman understands the Great Way,
And has no wish to be a mere worldly scholar.
The fine horses are already well-trained,
Beautiful robes shine with radiance.
With the left hand, I grasp the Fánruò bow,
With the right, I take the Wàngguī arrow.
Swift as the wind, vanishing like lightning,
Treading on shadows and chasing flight.
Galloping across the central plains,
Looking around with a spirited air.
Bringing along my good companions,
Carrying me in a light carriage.
To the south, we cross long ridges,
To the north, we pass through clear channels.
Looking up, we bring down the startled swan,
Looking down, we pull up fish from the deep.
Lingering in the pleasure of the hunt,
Its joy is indeed great.
The light carriage travels quickly,
We rest in that vast forest.
Spring trees are in full bloom,
Spreading their leaves and casting shade.
Gentle blows the valley wind,
Brushing against my plain qín.
Chirp, chirp, go the yellow birds,
Looking at their flock, they play their songs.
Moved to realization, my feelings race,
I think of the one I admire.
My heart is full of sorrow,
Forever sighing and chanting long.
Vast and wide is the great flood,
Girding the boundaries of my state.
Lush and green is the verdant forest,
Bursting with flowers and radiant light.
Fish and dragons break the surface,
Mountain birds fly in flocks.
I drive out for a journey,
Until evening, I forget to return.
I think of my good friend,
Like being thirsty or hungry.
Wishing for them and not obtaining,
How sorrowful is my grief.
Resting the followers in the orchid field,
pasturing horses on Huà Shān.
Skimming stones on the level marsh,
casting a line in the long river.
My eyes follow the returning wild geese,
my hands strum the five strings.
Looking up and down, I am content in myself,
my mind wanders in the Tài Xuán.
Admirable is that old fisherman,
who caught the fish and forgot the trap.
The man of Yǐng has passed away;
with whom can I speak my heart fully?
The quiet night is solemn and clear,
the bright moon shines on the porch.
A light breeze moves the lapels,
the silk curtains are pulled high.
Fine wine fills the goblet,
but there is no one to share the joy.
The sounding zither is ready,
but with whom can I play?
I admire those with similar interests,
whose fragrance is like the orchid.
The beautiful person is not here;
how can I not sigh forever!
Tall and slender are the Yǐ and Tóng trees,
growing on the Nán Yuè.
Above, they reach the blue clouds and rainbows;
below, they overlook a thousand-fathom valley.
Their position is lonely and precarious;
where shall I rest my feet?
Formerly planted on the sunny side,
their leaning branches awaited the Luán and Zhuó.
Now they are cut off from worldly use,
and I am constrained by haste and pressure.
Master Bān the craftsman does not look at me;
Yá and Kuàng do not notice me.
How can I be made into a zither or lute?
By what means can I raise a wonderful melody?
Gradually the three lights race away;
how quickly the passing time goes!
In the middle of the night, I cannot sleep;
touching my sword, I rise and pace about.
Moved by the sigh of the Sage Kǒng,
I lament that this life is so short.
Biàn Hé is hidden in the underworld;
who can testify to the rare jade?
I hope for the divine dragon to come,
and radiate light to illuminate me.
How pressing is the way of the official!
Constrained, I sit in self-confinement.
Cap strings and tassels are my bonds and fetters;
how can the laws and codes be overstepped?
Tranquility and vastness are bitterly lacking,
while vexation and haste are always in excess.
A good friend sends a new poem,
showing me amusement and play.
It is as solemn as a sprinkling cool breeze,
as brilliant as the blooming of spring flowers.
Since the past we were colleagues in the same bureau,
and now we are neighbors in gardens and huts.
In the evening of life, I am near disgrace and peril;
I hope we can retire together.
With hair loosened beneath the dense shade,
holding a staff, I approach the clear stream.
I lend an ear to hear the oriole’s song,
and let my eyes wander to watch the darting fish.
Leisurely I nourish my remaining days,
finding joy in the Sāngyú years.
The Great Potter molds all categories of things,
the Great Lump endows all living beings.
Light and dark indeed have different appearances;
stillness and agitation also have distinct forms.
From the time I gained consciousness,
my ambition was not in fame or merit.
Emptiness and tranquility were what I secretly loved,
but in literature and learning, I have experienced little.
Having unworthily accepted an excessive duty,
the white sun has already tilted to the west.
The way is long, but I suffer from short wisdom;
the responsibility is heavy, but I am troubled by light talent.
Zhōu Rèn has left behind a rule,
his words are clear and lucid.
Taking a high position while unfit is my warning;
vigilant by evening, I sit in self-alarm.
Thus, I am moved by your gracious gift,
expressing my heart with inner sincerity.
Though the opening lines are warm and beautiful,
do they not perhaps go against the true feeling?
The four seasons alternate and succeed each other,
the celestial bodies roll and unroll in turn.
Late spring suddenly returns,
and the gentle breeze comes with the season.
Looking down at the clear spring welling up,
looking up at the beautiful trees in bloom.
Strolling about my humble garden,
I look west toward the cottage at Guǎngwǔ.
Being noble yet not forgetting frugality,
possessing much yet able to live as if having nothing.
Calming the common ways through simplicity,
why should the excess of Shù Sài be followed?
In the past, we shared the same rank,
and now we are together in gardens and fields.
My private wish is to reach old age together,
wandering freely, occupied with zither and books.
Raising a goblet under the lush shade,
holding hands, together we linger.
Why bother with discarding the physical frame?
The trap is forgotten once the fish is caught.
Oh, majestic is the sagely era!
The culture of the times belongs to Jìn.
Receiving the mandate from Heaven,
it vastly possesses the wise and the common people.
The palace gates of Chānghé are already opened;
the Chénghuá Palace is established again.
Brilliant is the one who rules above;
those gathered there are only the virtuous.
Radiant is Master Féng,
whose wise inquiries truly follow the way.
Heaven’s protection settles you;
no virtue of yours is not glorious.
Pushing your heart into the profound and vast,
lifting your ambition to the high and distant.
Following toward that Chénghuá Palace,
your appearance is brilliantly bright.
Alas, for a person like me,
who folded his wings by the riverbank.
By command, I came to rest here,
flying up from the south.
Coming out from the dark valley,
I reached the same forest as you.
Our double sentiments reflect each other;
discarding worldly things, we know each other's heart.
People also have a saying:
the way of friendship is truly difficult.
There are those with hats standing tall,
but only once in a thousand years are the strings strummed.
Now I and you
share joy across generations.
Our bond is sharp enough to cut through metal and stone;
its aura is as kind as autumn orchids.
The common people are not yet pacified,
so the Emperor is diligent.
Seeking those of bright virtue
to extend over a hundred miles.
Everyone says you are in harmony,
letting the people follow your rule.
You turn your gaze to the north,
responding to and spreading the Emperor’s blessings.
Our travels of former days,
our pleasant union was deep and lingering.
Even if one says it was not yet complete,
it has already been three years.
Indoors, I accompanied you in the flowery tent;
outdoors, I followed your red-wheeled carriage.
Coupling our thoroughbreds, bits side-by-side,
we followed the same tracks in the same dust.
Since you have received the command,
the four stallions stretch their necks.
Following the path, treading far away,
galloping high on the tracks.
Auspicious clouds support your frame;
a cool breeze follows your image.
Alas, I think of the person
whose journey is so long.
If fortune and misfortune truly differ,
and poverty and success diverge,
while you are in your spring blossom,
I follow you like the autumn glow.
You are about to leave me
and ascend those northern frontiers.
If it were not for the thought of you,
for whom would my heart be sad?
Formerly, I was the Crown Prince’s Equerry.
Jiǎ Zhǎngyuān, as Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, was at the Eastern Palace for many years.
I went out to serve as the Palace Attendant of the Prince of Wú.
In the sixth year of Yuánkāng, I entered the capital to serve as a Gentleman of the Secretariat.
The Lǔ Gōng presented a poem to me,
and I composed this poem to answer him, and so forth.
In the past, there were sovereigns,
who first saved the common people.
They created things before Heaven and
received the Great Mandate.
Coming down to the various lords,
they rose and fell in succession.
Remote is the ancient past;
prosperity and decay have their proofs.
In the final years of the Hàn,
the imperial net was torn asunder.
The Dà Chén hid its brilliance,
and the Jīn Hǔ changed its nature.
Ambitious ministers galloped forth;
righteous men rushed to fulfill their duties.
Laying down positions and wielding spears,
they spoke of planning for the Royal House.
In the chaos of the Royal House,
no state was not ruined.
Like the setting sun,
it could never be raised again.
Then were regarded the three sages,
who governed these people.
Though opening the land was difficult,
they changed the institutions and succeeded Heaven.
Hereupon there was Wèi,
occupying the palace in the Heavenly City.
Wú indeed rose like a dragon,
and Liú also stood like a mountain peak.
Shields and spears were raised;
sacrificial vessels were stored away.
The people labored as the army rose;
the state toyed with entering in triumph.
Heaven tired of the hegemon's virtue;
the Yellow Lineage announced its end.
Lawsuits turned away from Wèi;
songs of praise went toward Jìn.
Chénliú returned to his fief;
our Emperor ascended through abdication.
Yōng and Mín bowed their heads;
Sān Jiāng changed its offerings.
Magnificent is the grand Jìn,
covering the entire land.
Responding to Heaven and men,
there is orderly blessing.
Verily, the Lord Tài Zǎi,
assisted and protected the two progenitors.
Born of a great lineage,
he continued the line in Lǔ.
Once the Eastern Court was established,
his fair reputation was lofty.
I sought his bright virtue,
achieving harmony through similarities.
The Duke of Lǔ arrived,
his ceremonial robes trailing.
Loving the Imperial Heir,
he walked high in the Chénghuá Palace.
When I first arrived here,
I was but a lowly official.
When you dwelled in seclusion,
we were in the same forest on different branches.
Though our years differed, our wills were comparable;
though our offices varied, our friendship was thick.
Roaming through three springs,
our feelings were as firm as two autumns.
Reverently receiving imperial orders,
coming and going without fail.
Going to serve in the princely court,
coming to walk in the Zǐ Wēi.
Rising and descending in the Mì Gé,
my robes shone with splendor.
Who would say I was not afraid?
I looked up in awe of the bright majesty.
To separate is easy,
but to hold hands is truly difficult.
Thinking of our fine travels of old,
I sigh deeply here!
The Duke, feeling moved,
sent me this letter of sound.
Elegant is that lofty writing,
like the luster of jade.
There is a tree in the Hàn region,
that does not cross the border.
There is gold in the south,
of which ten thousand nations sing.
What the people love in their hearts,
the wild and the cautious emulate the sage.
Your model was in the past;
I have heard your command.
Bound by the world and entangled in the net of the times,
I set out on a distant journey.
At the farewell banquet, who were the different clans?
All were relatives, brothers and kin.
Tenderly, those staying behind are in my thoughts;
pent up is the traveler's emotion.
At dawn, I lose my peaceful sleep;
waking up, tears soak my tassels.
Parting ways by the side of the Great Forest,
waving sleeves at the Wànshǐ Tíng.
Standing and gazing to catch a distant view,
leaning my ear to enjoy the lingering sounds.
Returning south to rest at Yǒng'ān,
journeying north to halt at Chéngmíng.
Yǒng'ān has yesterday's tracks,
but at Chéngmíng you have abandoned me.
Looking up and down, I grieve for the woods and thickets;
full of passion, I harbor bitterness.
Thinking of the past, joy is cut short;
mourning the future, sorrow becomes a thread.
Moved by the parting, I sadly spread my wings;
thinking of returning, I joyfully follow the riverbank.
The Dà Huǒ star fixes its vermilion light;
the accumulated Yáng shines from the south.
Wàng Shū leaves the Jīn Hǔ;
Píng Yì exhales heavy shadows.
Chilly winds go against the season's order;
bitter rain turns into a deluge.
Roaming in the morning, I forget my light feathers;
resting in the evening, I remember the heavy quilts.
Moved by things, a hundred sorrows arise,
entangled and following one after another.
Separated from you by a screen,
the screen is deep and distant.
Forms and shadows are far and do not meet;
what is relied upon are sounds and news.
Sounds and news grow more distant day and night;
what can I use to comfort my heart?
Roaming in the morning at the tiered city;
returning in the evening to the duty quarters.
Sudden thunder rumbles in the midnight;
startling lightning flashes in the night.
Dark clouds trail over the vermilion pavilions;
shaking winds buffet the patterned lattice.
Heavy downpours overflow the long eaves;
yellow muddy water soaks the steps.
Settled shadows gather and do not dissipate;
the thoroughfares are transformed into canals.
Sunken crops are buried in the Liáng and Yǐng;
displaced people flow toward Jīng and Xú.
Looking back with thoughts of my homeland,
would they not all become fish!
Gù Hóu embodies bright virtue;
his pure wind has already spread.
Starting his career assisting the princely lord,
he was reassigned to soothe the southern borders.
Beating drums beyond the Wǔ Lǐng;
raising banners ten thousand lǐ away.
Distant achievements do not decline for being small;
establishing virtue does not depend on greatness.
How could high mountains be enough to climb over?
Even the great sea is like a sash.
Melancholy, I watch your departing carriage;
craning my neck, I look for your returning banner.
A lone beast yearns for its old thicket;
a stray bird grieves for its old forest.
Flitting about is the traveling official;
for whom does his heart suffer hardship?
Dimly appearing on the sunny side of Gǔ Shuǐ;
tenderly on the shady side of Kūn Shān.
My soul yearns for this land;
my spirit seems to fly or sink.
Awake or asleep, I find no peace or joy;
in my words, I think of the one I admire.
Moved by the hardships of the return journey,
it makes my longing and admiration deep.
How can I obtain the grass of forgetting-return,
to plant it by my back and lapel?
How could these words be made in vain?
The pining bird has a sorrowful sound.
Keeping myself pure, I ascended the Mì Gé;
the Mì Gé is lofty and profound.
All morning I manage documents;
by dusk, I have no time to sleep.
I set out to inspect the bright sacrifices,
paying respect in prayers for the year.
Wandering in the Spring Garden of the Sovereign,
pacing through the Qiānmǔ Tián.
Winding canals encircle the curved paths;
flowing waves support the straight trails.
Fine grains hang with double ears;
fragrant trees blossom at their tops.
I am originally a man of the water country;
holding the reins, I overlook the clear depths.
Full of grief and many distant thoughts,
as I walk, these verses have formed a poem.
Leaving home to travel far away,
for a long and distant three thousand lǐ.
Jīng Luò is filled with much wind and dust,
and my white robes have turned to black.
Cultivating my character, I grieve over sorrows and hardships,
feeling deep thoughts for my brothers.
Deep contemplations depart from the core of my heart,
and sunken joys linger without rising.
When joy is sunken, it is difficult to rouse;
with a mind in turmoil, who can set it in order?
I wish to borrow the wings of a returning swan,
to soar back to the banks of the Zhèjiāng.
In the southeast, there is a pining wife,
her long sighs fill the secluded gateway.
May I ask what those sighs are for?
Her fair one is far away at the edge of the sky!
Traveling on official duty, he has not returned for a long time,
and the mountains and rivers are distant and wide.
Forms and shadows are parted like the stars Shēn and Shāng,
news and letters are rare and do not arrive.
Union and separation do not have a constant rule,
but are like the bowstring and the arrow's notch.
I hope you preserve your body of gold and stone,
to comfort my long hunger and thirst!
Formerly with two or three companions,
I wandered and rested south of Chénghuá.
Flapping our wings on the same branch,
we have now flown apart to different heights.
Lacking the pinions to brave the wind,
I linger and guard the old forest.
Who is moved by these fervent feelings?
I speak my thoughts of the one I admire.
Setting out from the banks of the Qīng Luò,
driving my horse by the north of the Dà Hé.
Standing still to gaze at the northern road,
it is distant, remote, and deep.
Separation has been a sorrow since ancient times,
and a man of ambition has many bitter thoughts.
Sorrowful feelings gather by the river,
and bitter words are chanted with the wind.
I am ashamed to have no jade pendants to give,
but good news shall replace fine gold.
You, sir, possess grand and far-reaching plans;
I send my sincere heart in these kind words.
Go now, though I resent the long road,
grieving that the parting is so hurried.
Pointing to the path, sorrow is more than enough;
facing the wine, joy is insufficient.
I am like water flowing to the west,
while you are the mountain standing in the east.
Fervent feelings are moved at the moment of departure,
and lingering emotions grow in our dwelling.
How can we hold hands together,
bound like the team of horses for a carriage?
From the very beginning of creation,
the two forces of heaven and earth were in flux.
Then there were the living people,
and Fúxī was the first to rule.
He knotted cords to spread civilization,
and the eight trigrams became the script.
Vast were the nine provinces,
as the regions were divided.
Shénnóng reigned next,
and Xuānyuán continued the record.
Mapping the wilds and separating boundaries,
he then enfeoffed many sons.
After the Xià and Yīn had succeeded each other,
the ancestral Zhōu continued the sacrifices.
Like the continuous growth of melons on the vine,
the Six States stood against one another.
Powerful Qín annexed them all,
swallowing the four corners of the earth.
Zǐyīng surrendered with a coffin,
and Hànzǔ received the mandate.
Emperors Líng and Xiàn were weak,
like white silk being dyed and changed.
Three heroes stood like the legs of a tripod,
and Sūn established Nán Wú.
What was this Nán Wú?
It usurped the title and called itself a kingdom.
Great Jìn unified all under heaven,
its benevolent wind spreading far.
The false Sūn held the jade in his mouth,
offering his lands and returning his borders.
Graceful is the Cháng Lí,
soaring across the river.
Who is this Cháng Lí?
It is you, Lù Shēng.
A crane cries in the nine marshes,
yet its voice is still heard.
How much more so from the corner of the sea,
spreading your name to the Upper Capital.
Responding to the summons of the banners,
you serve in the halls of government.
A choice for the Crown Prince's staff,
truly selected for your excellence.
Brilliant is the vermillion phoenix,
coming from the southern hills.
Shining with literary grace and upholding the right,
wearing the black cap and red robes.
Like the orchids and irises,
their fragrance is gathered.
Serving as a bulwark in the provinces,
assisting our capital house.
Returning again to your home village,
the Emperor's brother served as assistant.
Some say officialdom in the states
is where the pure path is lost.
But you, sir, are refreshed,
tranquil and naturally at ease.
The court is pure,
inviting men of talent.
Promoted in response to a fine recommendation,
you moved from your state.
Riding alongside the dragons,
gloriously assisting the Secretariat.
Strolling through the government offices,
carrying a brush in the decorated halls.
Formerly, I and you
were close in the Eastern Court.
Though treated with the ritual of guests,
our feelings were those of friends and colleagues.
Enjoying the music of strings and flutes,
beating the drums and dancing to the Sháo.
On bright days and under clear moons,
we walked hand in hand in leisure.
Since I left the group,
two cycles have passed until now.
Though we have seldom seen each other face to face,
our deep feelings are clearly known.
You are transcendent indeed,
truly a comfort to my heart.
I express these words in a poem,
waiting to hear good news from you.
To make a height grand,
one must value its layers.
The handle for establishing virtue
is nothing other than peace and constancy.
In the south, it is called a sweet tangerine;
moved to the north, it becomes a bitter orange.
I prize your sharp brilliance;
may it never falter or crumble.
The beauty of the Southeast
was formerly only Yánzhōu.
Illustrious and faithful Lù Shēng,
you have few peers today.
Shaking your scales in the Southern Sea,
washing your wings in the clear stream.
Dancing in the forest of letters,
lingering among the ancient mounds.
Jade is enriched by its luster,
the Suí pearl shines with radiance.
Thus you gradually reached the Upper Capital,
and served in the palace of the Crown Prince.
I enjoy your pure literary grace,
and savor your fragrant character.
The more one swims in it, the wider it becomes;
the more one draws from it, the deeper it feels.
What is found on Kūnlún Mountain?
There is fine jade and precious gems.
Along with your colleagues,
you are all close ministers.
I have entered the plain autumn of my life,
while you ascend in your youth.
I am ashamed to have no mature wisdom
to join those who renew themselves daily.
Grand and numerous is the great state,
with its mulberries and catalpas.
Solemn and dignified is this man,
the pillar of the Southern Land.
The Emperor said, "You are fit
to be a minister to the King."
Bowing low to follow the command,
you care for your duty—how could it be for mere joy?
My carriage is already covered,
my horse is already fed.
Under the stars, I prepare the morning drive,
greasing the wheels and fixing the axle-pin.
Attached to the two palaces,
I linger by the gates of the hall.
The clear wine is not enjoyed;
who can comfort this hunger and thirst?
Formerly, you were kind to me,
giving me orchids and irises.
Now you are going to the east,
what can I give you as a gift?
An inch of time is most precious;
is it not better than fine jade?
That beautiful Lù Shēng
is one with whom I can speak face to face.
Mì Shēng transformed Dānfù,
Zǐqí presided over Dōng'é.
At Tóngxiāng, a legacy of merit was established,
At Wǔchéng, the sound of strings and song was spread.
A swift steed gallops upon the level road,
A submerged dragon leaps in the great waves.
At twenty, he walked among the high ministers,
Once established, he governed Sānhé.
His flowing reputation is as fragrant as autumn orchids,
His displayed compositions are as radiant as spring flowers.
It is merely beautiful that his natural grace is lush,
How could one say his human rank is excessive?
Kūnshān amasses fine jade,
A great mansion is constructed from many timbers.
Swimming fish gather in the numinous pond,
With folded wings, they hope for the heavenly stairs.
For what does the oil-soaked orchid consume itself?
Bringing order to governance depends on the worthy and capable.
Princes and marquises weary of lofty rituals,
They turn their steps toward the pure Xiàntái.
The inchworm’s contraction is surely a small departure,
The dragon’s flight is thus a great arrival.
With united hearts, they assist the sagely era,
With all their strength, they praise the era of peace!
Lord Hé Jìngzǔ of Lǎnglíng,
Is the maternal elder cousin of Xián;
Wáng Wǔzǐ, the Libationer of the Imperial Academy,
Is the grandson of Xián’s paternal aunt.
Both are held in high esteem by the world for their bright virtue,
Xián is close to them and values them;
In affection, they are like brothers born of the same womb,
In righteousness, they are teachers and friends.
After Lord Hé ascended to the position of Palace Attendant,
Wǔzǐ soon after also took the post.
The two worthies find great joy in each other,
Xián also celebrates them.
However, I personally regret my own ignorance and inferiority,
Though I wish for their deep attachment,
There is no way for me to follow them;
Successive trials have yielded no effect,
And moreover, I face family hardships.
I compose these poems to express my feelings,
And present them to them, and so it is said.
The sun and moon illuminate the Tàiqīng,
The constellations shine upon the Zǐwēi.
Resplendent is the court of the Great Jìn,
Brightly, the imperial gates are opened.
My elder brother has soared like a phoenix,
Prince Wáng has also flown like a dragon.
A pair of simurghs wanders by the orchid islets,
Two Lí birds radiate pure light.
Hand in hand, they ascend the jade stairs,
Side by side, they sit attending the cinnabar curtain.
Golden pendants adorn their huìwén caps,
Brilliantly, they reveal their excellent bearing.
Such glory is not what I can hope for,
Yet deep attachment is what my heart desires.
How could I not aspire to their high tracks,
But the unicorn’s footprints are distant and hard to follow.
Facing the stream, I have no fragrant bait,
Why should I stay in vain upon the islet?
Withered leaves wait for the wind to blow,
Soon I shall depart from you.
Departing from you, how could I not feel longing?
Occupying a post in vain, I ought to say I shall return.
Returning myself to a humble cottage of thatch,
To delight in the Way and forget my hunger.
In advancement, I have no contribution to speak of,
In retreat, I shall care for my private affairs.
I only wish that your vast beauty flourishes,
And the King’s regulations become daily more peaceful and serene.
Bright and pure is the white raw silk,
Woven to make garments for a poor woman.
Though the poor woman is subtle and skillful,
She is not allowed to hold the loom’s shuttle.
In the cold of the year, one knows how fast time moves,
How much more so when the wild geese fly south.
The master tailor holds the blade and ruler,
But casts me aside as if forgotten.
If people do not take from their own persons,
What could the scholars of this world hope for?
Moreover, having already eaten their morning meal,
By what means could they know my hunger?
Far and long is your journey,
Desolate and alone, I remain behind.
How can mountains and rivers be crossed?
The long road is separated by ten thousand lǐ.
In the capital chambers are many seductive beauties,
Radiant are the daughters of the city folk.
With elegant steps, they lift their slender waists,
With artful smiles, they reveal their white teeth.
Such fine beauties are truly lovely,
How could a withered and lowly one be worth mentioning?
From afar, I receive your words of concern,
Harboring a gratitude that was not expected from the start.
One who has floated on the sea finds other waters difficult,
One who has wandered in the forests finds other sights difficult.
Appearance and color are valued when in season,
The morning flower fears the late sun.
Bright and clear is that beautiful lady,
Resplendent, she harbors the brilliance of spring.
In Xīchéng, they are good at elegant dances,
In Zǒngzhāng, there is much pure strumming.
Sounding reeds come from cinnabar lips,
Vermilion strings wind around white wrists.
Light skirts are like the flash of lightning,
Paired sleeves are like the scattering mist.
Flowery countenances overflow the patterned curtains,
Mournful echoes enter the Cloudy Han.
One who knows the tone is rare in this world,
Other than you, who could praise it?
Cast aside the Northern Star,
And ask of this brilliant Dark Dragon’s radiance.
The season is late, what more is there to say?
When the flowers fall, they must by reason be lowly.
A distant path can eventually be reached,
But a brief parting makes the resentment of waiting feel long.
Harboring gratitude, I long for your journey,
I give rise to words while facing the wine cup.
At the southern ferry, there is a crossing cut off,
At the northern islet, there is no river bridge.
In spirit I go with you, sharing the same feeling of passing,
In form I remain, saddened like Shēn and Shāng.
If our tracks diverge like the yoke and the wheel,
The Qiānniú star does not pull the carriage box.
Your journey crosses the long river,
Drifting and tossing, braving the wind and dust.
Flowing waves surge against the crooked islets,
Sorrowful winds press against the hill’s thickets.
On the long road, there are endless tracks,
Wells and hamlets follow one after another.
A hundred cities each have different customs,
A thousand households do not provide a good neighbor.
Old joys are hard to match by chance,
Can the local customs be truly intimate?
I feel longing for the city of my home,
Appearing as if the people are before my eyes.
Gradually, day and night, you draw further away,
With devoted heart, I harbor bitterness and hardship.
Kūn kowtows:
You have sent your letter and poems,
which are filled with bitter and agonizing words
and express a profound and far-reaching intent.
I have read them over and over,
unable to let them out of my hands.
I am moved to sigh with sorrow,
yet I feel a sense of joy.
In my youth,
I never practiced self-restraint.
From afar, I admired the "Equalization of Things" of Lǎozǐ and Zhuāngzǐ;
more closely, I appreciated the unrestrained freedom of Master Ruǎn.
I used to wonder where the distinction between depth and shallowness of feeling came from,
and what caused grief and joy to arrive?
Recently, amidst the chaos and upheaval,
I have been exhausted by rebellion and disorder.
The state is ruined and my family is gone;
my relatives and friends have withered away.
Leaning on my staff and chanting poems,
a hundred sorrows arrive all at once.
Sitting alone in solitude,
grief and indignation both gather.
Occasionally, we raise our cups and face each other knee-to-knee again,
turning tears into laughter,
dispelling the accumulated misery of a lifetime,
and seeking a few moments of temporary joy.
This is like a chronic illness that has lasted for years,
which one hopes to cure with a single pill—
can that truly be achieved?
Talent is born into the world,
and the world indeed needs talent.
As for the jade of Master Hé,
how could it shine only in the hands of the people of Yǐng?
As for the luminous pearl,
how could it be enjoyed exclusively in the palm of the Marquis of Suí?
The treasures of the world
should be shared with the world.
But on the day of separation,
one cannot help but feel regret!
Only then did I realize that Dān
and Zhōu were empty and boastful,
and that Sìzōng’s conduct was reckless.
Formerly, when the Lùjì steed leaned against the carriage shaft on the slope of Wú,
it neighed toward Liáng Lè—
it is a matter of being recognized or not.
Bǎilǐ Xī was foolish in Yú but wise in Qín—
it is a matter of meeting the right opportunity or not.
Now you have met your opportunity,
so just exert yourself!
I have not set my mind to writing for over twenty years.
After long neglect, there is no coherence;
I thought you would surely want a response,
so I have composed this piece according to your theme,
which is only enough to highlight the superior beauty of your own poem.
Kūn kowtows, kowtows.
Misfortune first met me,
when the Yang line was at the six.
In the Qián image, the ridgepole tilted;
in the Kūn form, the boat capsized.
Turbulence and confusion arose,
as various demons vied with each other.
Fire blazed across Shénzhōu,
and a great flood surged through the Huá region.
Those millet plants are lush,
that grain is growing thick.
I grieve for our Imperial Jìn,
the heartbreak is before my eyes.
Heaven and Earth have no heart,
all things follow the same path.
Punishment for the wicked is not verified,
and blessings for the good are empty.
Rebellious ones hold whole towns,
while the righteous have no intact capital.
Heroic blossoms fall in summer,
while poisonous plants bloom in winter.
Like the tortoise shells and jade,
destroyed within their caskets.
The talk of "straw dogs"—
is that perhaps the most accurate?
I sigh at my own weakness,
unable to bear the burden.
My faults and offenses are continually revealed,
yet honors and favors are repeatedly added.
Because my authority was not established,
disaster spread and evil was sown.
Loyalty failed the state,
and filial piety was lacking in the family.
The accumulation of these sins
is like the mountains and rivers.
The depth of this offense
can never be erased.
My refined old relatives,
and the gentle new marriage ties.
Packing provisions and carrying the weak,
we fled like falling stars.
Before you had stopped your carriage,
my house had already been destroyed.
Both families perished together,
the three evils rooted together.
Always ashamed before the old orphans,
eternally indebted to the wronged souls.
A tall and solitary trunk,
growing alone without a companion.
The green leaves were lush and dense,
but the tender branches were long and sparse.
In the morning I gathered your fruit,
in the evening I stroked your stem.
The green stem was many fathoms long,
and extraordinary pearls filled the bowl.
It truly dispelled my sorrow,
making the urgent anxiety ease.
Are you now going away?
The courtyard is empty, yet my heart is full.
What of this emptiness and fullness?
The orchid and cassia are transplanted.
Lush are those spring forests,
withered are these autumn thorns.
A bird flies up and away,
with no time to rest.
It perches on nothing but the paulownia,
it eats nothing but the bamboo.
It forever folds its eastern feathers,
and strokes its western wings.
Out of my respect for him,
I set aside joy and neglected my duties.
Music is played for those who appreciate it,
flavors are for those who savor rare delicacies.
Writing is to clarify speech,
speech is to express the spirit.
Now that you are going,
the four beauties will not arrive.
Clear wine is poured out,
strings and flutes gather dust.
Plain scrolls are not opened,
and the curtains host no talking guests.
Having isolated my virtue,
and also left my neighborhood vacant.
Illustrious Master Duàn,
emerging from the valley to move to the heights.
Endowed with loyalty and treading in sincerity,
martial brilliance and literary splendor.
The decorated bows are strong,
the carriages and horses are grand.
Now you exert the long reins,
handling the bridle and bit.
What shall I give to you?
Exhaust your heart at the imperial court.
How shall I express my feelings?
I crane my neck and sing a long song.
In my hand I hold a hanging jade disc,
originally a gem from Jīngshān.
Consider that Tàigōng Wàng,
was formerly an old man on the banks of the Wèi.
How inspired Master Dèng was,
coming from a thousand miles to seek a lord.
Báidēng relied on Qūniè,
and the Hóng Gate relied on the Marquis of Liú.
Zhòng’ěr employed the Five Worthies,
Xiǎobái made a minister of the one who shot at his buckle.
If one can make the two Hegemons prosper,
why ask about partisans or enemies?
At midnight I stroke my pillow and sigh,
wishing to roam with those several gentlemen.
I have been declining for a long time,
why do I no longer dream of the Duke of Zhōu?
Who says the sage attains the Way,
and knowing fate, therefore does not worry?
Xuāní grieved at the capture of the lín,
hunting in the west, Kǒng Qiū wept.
Before great achievements could be established,
the setting sun suddenly flows to the west.
Time does not wait for me,
departing like floating clouds.
Red fruits fall in the strong wind,
dense blossoms drop in the plain autumn.
On a narrow road, the flowery canopy tilts,
startled horses break the double shafts.
Who would have thought that steel refined a hundred times,
could be turned into something soft enough to wrap around a finger.
Your former subordinate and Attendant Gentleman of the Middle, Lú Chén, commits a capital offense, a capital offense!
Chén’s natural disposition is limited and weak,
and he is seldom fit for the responsibilities of the age.
Following his natural state,
he finds peace in stillness and withdrawal.
He has the quality of useless lumber among trees,
and possesses the lot of the goose that lacks a fine call.
His withdrawal differs from that of Qú zǐ;
his foolishness is distinct from that of Nìng Shēng.
The master craftsman occasionally cast a glance upon him,
and so he could not avoid being a guest at the feast.
He once reflected to himself
that through the meeting of circumstances and fortune,
he was favored to be accepted into service,
personally attending upon your pure presence
for five years until now.
No results of brilliant counsel have been manifested,
yet the ridicule of the "Waiters" has become apparent.
Your great virtue is magnanimous and grand,
your capacity encompassing mountains and marshes.
Furthermore, your treatment of me became increasingly excellent,
and your sincere affection grew ever more intimate;
I participated in the strategies of planning
and was admitted to the joys of private banquets.
The depth of your kind intent
was like that toward your own flesh and blood;
as for your being "one who knows me,"
even the ancients could not provide a comparison.
In the past, Niè Zhèng sacrificed himself for the regard of Yán Suì,
and Jīng Kē admired the righteousness of Yàn Dān.
In a moment of spirited conviction,
they destroyed their bodies without regret.
Although I lack such lofty principles,
I believe I might aspire to them.
However, if it be said that one has feelings,
who could fail to harbor such thoughts?
Therefore, on the day I committed my person to you,
I already regarded ease and danger as one.
But matters have gone against my wishes,
and I must shamefully take up an external post;
thus, I leave your side
and withdraw my steps from the government office.
Because the origin is the same but the ends differ,
Yáng Zhū gave rise to sorrow;
because it begins white but ends black,
Mò Dí shed tears.
At the moment of separation and divergence,
all may sigh and lament;
the paths that lead to such feelings
perhaps are compelled by this very situation.
Why must one wait to be at the roadside before wailing aloud,
or see the silk threads before sobbing?
Therefore, looking up to reflect on past sentiments,
and looking down to survey current circumstances,
I am moved by the living and remember the departed;
whatever I touch fills me with longing.
The Yì says:
"Writing does not fully express words;
words do not fully express meaning."
If this is so, then writing is not the vessel for fully expressing words,
and words are not the instrument for fully expressing meaning.
How much more so when words cannot reach the fullness of meaning,
and writing cannot reach the fullness of words?
I cannot overcome my humble distress!
I respectfully present one poem;
though it is insufficient to extol your grand beauty,
it is merely to express what I hold in my heart.
If Your Excellency would extend great kindness
and fulfill your profound grace
by bestowing the sounds of your own voice
to console these thoughts of separation,
it would be what is called the Xiánchí music responding to the Běilǐ,
or a night-glowing pearl repaying a fish's eye.
This is Chén’s wish,
though it is not something I dare to expect.
Chén commits a capital offense, a capital offense.
Deeply wise is the Emperor,
who succeeded and expanded the great Jìn.
He revitalized the slackened bonds of state,
and illustriously spread a far-reaching grace.
There come those in harmony,
reaching this place in perfect accord.
The Sāntái shed their brilliance,
and the Sìyuè peaks increase in majesty.
Yī Zhì assisted Shāng,
Shān Fǔ supported Zhōu.
Greatly they aided in times of hardship,
responding to and extolling the King's excellence.
Were it not for their exceptional virtue,
how could they join the same stream across generations?
Adding to this their loyalty and integrity,
they proclaimed their illustrious path.
I, Shèn, come from a humble clan,
and in the past encountered your kind favor.
Renewed through ties of marriage,
and made manifest through successive generations.
In duty, we share joys and sorrows;
in affection, we are one in rise and fall.
Who says we are not in harmony?
Like the perfect accord of music!
The Royal House lost its hosts,
and private families were uprooted and moved.
Looking toward your return,
regarding dangers as nothing and ignoring hardships.
This wish was not fulfilled,
for the path was blocked and overturned midway.
Looking up, I grieve for former intentions;
looking down, I reflect on my own transgressions.
The Great Potter's Wheel turns again,
and the auspicious days have passed away.
Gazing upon those sun and moon,
they pass swiftly in the blink of an eye.
Moved by the present while thinking of the past,
the mouth speaks of it, the heart dwells on it.
Even if one says it was like yesterday,
suddenly it has become days of old.
What of those days of old?
Those who have passed grow more distant.
Gentle and reverent person,
careful at the end as at the beginning.
Reviewing those remaining words,
pitying this destitute orphan.
Like that drooping tree,
upon which the creeping kudzu spreads.
How marvelous is the creeping kudzu,
to find support upon the drooping tree.
Its leaves do not spread like clouds,
its flowers do not shine like stars.
Receiving treatment equal to Biàn Hé,
though my substance is not the uncut jade of Jīng.
Favored as if among the most excellent,
yet lacking the talent of the finest steeds.
The support received is already profound,
and the favor shown is already intimate;
You polished and encouraged this slow and lowly one,
to drive alongside the swiftest and most precious.
Assistance in harmony has not been achieved,
and fine counsel has not been presented.
I do not hope to rival Hú and Zhào,
yet I was among the five ministers.
Who were the five ministers?
Those who shared hardships through a hundred tribulations.
My person experienced dangers and obstacles,
my feet trod through the dark and distant.
Duty arises from deep kindness,
and our bond increased with intimacy.
Bound together in heart and soul,
considering ourselves as one, not as others.
Formerly, in days of leisure,
we subtly sought the universal truths.
Especially valuing that spirit and character,
which makes one a man of integrity.
Emotion is born from the essence,
and feeling arises from emotion.
In taking or leaving there is no fixed rule,
it is simply a matter of failure or success.
A single word from Yóu Yú
was what the people of Qín feared.
Rìdī demonstrated his loyalty,
his fame soaring through the Hàn.
The martial Fǔjūn
was the crown among ancient worthies.
He came to govern Yōu Dū,
and rescued the people from the mire.
Once the misery was relieved,
the bandits were crushed and the people prospered.
Mistakenly, this exhausted servant
was granted a high place in the court.
Above, I fear the greatness of the responsibility;
below, I rejoice in the depth of the favor.
Truly I revere your lofty brilliance;
how could I dare forget what I maintain?
Look at the bird that feeds its parents in return;
even among the winged creatures it exists.
Who is such a person
that could bear to have such a heart?
Always relying on the mountains and seas,
hoping to behold their height and depth.
Looking afar at survival and death,
they have long since become the soaring and the sinking.
The long tassels are already tied,
and soon I shall move and depart.
Gathering my steps to tread westward,
I harbor grief while looking back to the east.
How can it be said the road is far?
It is not even a few short steps.
Do I not think of morning and night?
But they say the path is heavy with dew.
Extending far is the lady-cross vine,
attached to the crown of the pine tree.
Receiving moisture from the great trunk,
drying in the sun upon the lush branches.
With shallow roots, it is hard to be firm;
with weak stems, it is easy to wither.
Maintaining that slender substance,
it encounters this rushing gale.
The slender substance is indeed minute,
and the rushing gale is what it meets.
Who says the words are refined?
Their effect lies in the appreciation of the meaning.
One who does not see the fish
also forgets the bait.
Leaving behind the physical frame,
I entrust myself to deep understanding.
The people of old nurtured their minds,
hiding in the mountains, leaning on their mats.
Looking up to enjoy the vermilion cliffs,
looking down to wash in the green waters.
Without seeking for harmony,
they naturally attached themselves to all things beautiful.
Though fervent about those distant traces,
I feel ashamed before those lofty ideals.
Thus, different theories were created,
making liver and gall as distant as Chǔ and Yuè.
But if one looks with the Great Vision,
the ten thousand differences follow a single track.
Since life and death are equalized,
what distinction is there between glory and shame?
Resting at the mysterious root,
all is vast and without entanglement.
Fortune is the beginning of calamity;
calamity is the stepping stone to fortune.
Heaven and earth wax and wane;
cold and heat come and go in a cycle.
Fū Chāi receives no sacrifices;
his fault lay in defeating Qí.
Gōu Jiàn became a hegemon;
his blessing began at Kuàijī.
Far-reaching is the enlightened perspective;
only the Dào is to be relied upon.
Though the physical form may not be at ease,
the spirit is nowhere uninhibited.
Like the flowing of a river,
like the capacity of an abyss.
Above, he expands the greatness of a pillar of state;
below, he fulfills the expectations of the people.
Leisurely I stroll by the corner of the city wall,
in days of ease, finding a bit of pleasure.
To the north, I gaze at the edge of the desert;
to the south, I look toward the road to the old capital.
The level plains draw along the long streams;
the hills and ridges stand with lush trees.
On the central plains, a fierce gale rages;
in the mountain bends, clouds and mists arise.
The traveler always harbors a sorrowful heart;
looking up, his eternal longing increases.
Good companions cannot be joined together;
to whom shall I tell my unfolding feelings?
Far-off I think of the manner of worthy men,
and thus dwell on the affairs of antiquity.
The northern borders are full of heroic spirit;
is it only because of the nature of the land?
Lǐ Mù guarded the frontier cities,
and the wild tribes harbored fear of the south.
Zhào Shē set the battlefields in order,
and the people of Qín abandoned their plans for the north.
As a traveler, I encountered a lenient government,
dedicating myself as I met with the times.
My regret is that with the nature of a slow and limping horse,
I have in vain troubled a master driver like Fēizǐ to guide me.
Having already laid down my heavy burden,
I once shamefully held the post of governing the common people.
If I can be said to have escaped guilt and blame,
what leisure would I have to gather the people's praise?
Ní Kuān was dismissed for being at the bottom of the rankings,
yet in the end, his tax collection was the highest.
Hé Wǔ was not illustriously famous,
yet the love he left behind remained after he was gone.
The ancients are not what I can hope to equal;
being short of talent and weak has always been my nature.
Why do I set forth these words?
It is solely because of those two gentlemen.
A lofty terrace is not made of a single timber;
a precious fur is not made from a single armpit.
Many scholars achieve great undertakings;
a crowd of worthies accomplishes grand success.
Encountering the chance of fortune's arrival,
I briefly joined the ranks of the court's elites.
Looking back at these wings on my back,
I feel ashamed before those who soar through the void.
Entrusting my person to the shade of the *Sìyuè*,
relying on the friendship of the "three benefits."
Though our meeting was as brief as a passing carriage,
our great bond surpasses that of old acquaintances.
In danger, we always shared the same perils;
in safety, we did not treat ease differently.
Together we traversed the hardships of *Jìnchāng*;
together we endured the calamities of *Fēihú*.
Kindness arises from shared labor;
righteousness accumulates through long association.
Who would have thought that the reputation from my village
would mistakenly fill the duties of my home province?
Our separation moves me with emotion;
sorrow and joy make my feelings tremble.
Reason communicates through the spirit;
it is not said to be separated by physical bodies.
Exquisite poems express deep affection;
pure principles penetrate the obscure and profound.
I regret having no Pearl of *Suíhóu*
to repay the Jade of *Jīngwén*.
The evening clears and the air is cool;
the quiet room has a lingering purity.
Opening the window and extinguishing the bright candle,
the white moonlight and dew are already full.
Alone at night with no worldly burdens,
the sleeper is also at peace.
Suddenly I receive the song of "Sorrowful Rain,"
and with effort, I play what was composed.
Sighing at the hardships of the traveler,
deeply moved by these affectionate words.
Though I have little to comfort me,
my heavy worries briefly become light.
Constrained to respond with fine lines,
I bow long, ashamed of my life.
Branches are numerous and the forest is lush;
waves are clear and the source is deep.
My illustrious clan gave birth to our talent;
you, sir, continue the ancestral line.
Intimately bound by refined character,
the misty fragrance emits news of your virtue.
Rising like a swan according to circumstances;
the *Yúntái* grows loftier with the years.
Flowers and calyxes brighten each other;
chirping birds delight in the same sound.
Treating kin as kin, you are generous to me;
honoring the worthy, I appreciate you.
Comparing shadows, the latter has little brilliance;
comparing years, you are one day older.
Withering leaves love flourishing branches;
parched streams like the vastness of the river.
Sacrificing for work, I lack successful conduct;
returning to ritual, I am ashamed of my "joy in poverty."
Fortunately meeting the time to serve in office,
I was tasked with governing the bends of *Jiāngnán*.
Moving through time, I grieve its fleeting nature;
following the road, I sigh at its vast distance.
Spreading my heart to remember the one I admire,
how intense is my toil!
Though we initially shared the same purpose,
we fly off in different manners.
Distant beyond the imperial borders,
deep within the *Chéngmíng* Hall.
Following paths that have already diverged;
reaching principles that have already met.
The silken path has constant sorrow,
let alone when it concerns my beloved.
Walking a short distance with steady steps;
clipped wings circling a few fathoms.
Is it that I don't know the high and far?
Deviating from the path brings regret.
In the cold of the year, frost and snow are severe;
halfway through, the road becomes steeper.
Assessing myself, I fear my friends;
courageously withdrawing, I dare not advance.
Go now, and strive for an excellent reputation;
I write my sincerity to respond to your message.
My journey was planned for the first month of spring;
in mid-spring, I have yet to depart.
The distant path has a set date;
the feeling of parting never ceases.
Having prepared my luggage, I wait for a lucky day;
launching the boat in the pleasant month of *Táo*.
Looking at the path, my heart has little joy;
looking back, my feelings are full of loss.
My wise elder brother is moved by our parting;
he sees me off beyond the suburban forest.
Drinking together at the pavilion in the wilds;
parting ways in the shade of the clear lake.
Sorrowful are the words you leave me;
lingering is the heart of the traveler.
The winding embankment hides the oars;
looking afar, form and sound are cut off.
Moving slowly onto the long road;
mournfully harboring distant grief.
Distant grief can only be suppressed by oneself;
on the long road, to whom should I speak?
Walking and walking, the way grows further;
going and going, my heart lingers more.
Yesterday I set out from the bend of *Pǔyáng*;
today I lodge at the bank of the *Zhèjiāng*.
Heavy clouds shroud the high peaks;
startling winds surge through the flying current.
Drizzling rain moistens the graves and marshes;
falling snow sprinkles the woods and hills.
Floating mist darkens the cliffs and peaks;
accumulated whiteness confuses the plains and fields.
At the curved bank, the travelers briefly stop;
on the main river, moving boats are cut off.
Arriving at the ferry but unable to cross;
resting the oars, blocked by wind and waves.
Desolate are the shores and islets;
the colors of the air have little harmony.
Looking west, I sigh at my travels;
looking east, I break into a mournful song.
Accumulated resentment becomes an illness;
without the *xuān* herb, what shall I do?
Resigning when full—is it for a high salary?
Excusing myself due to illness, I did not wait for old age.
By chance, I match the paths of *Zhāng* and *Bìng*;
long have I wished to return to *Dōngshān*.
The Sacred Spirit once looked upon me with favor;
my humble intentions were not yet declared.
How could I expect the rushing gale to stir,
and the fierce fire to release flaming smoke?
Burning the jade that comes from *Kūnlún* peaks;
by the remaining embers, I was finally moved.
Cast into the sands, the situation is pressing;
like reaching *Qióng*, my wishes are also thwarted.
Forever parting from those I love;
eternally severing the bonds of my life.
Floating a boat in a thousand-fathom gorge;
grasping the reins on a ten-thousand-fathom peak.
Flowing foam is not dangerous enough;
how can a stone forest be a hardship?
How can one reside in *Mǐnzhōng*?
Day and night, I think of returning.
Matters are obstructed yet both remain upright;
the heart is content, thrice yielding to the worthy.
Placing myself above the blue clouds;
dwelling on cliffs, sipping from flying springs.
Flourishing brilliance washes away the gloom;
true excellence soothes the difficulties.
All distant regions receive grace;
even lowly things are selected in advance.
Deeply moved, my resolve is not firm;
my nature is weak and easily bound.
Now that I have returned to my former garden,
speaking of the past is truly sincere.
The previous foundation was built by ancestors;
the old pond is not dug anew.
Fruit trees are in their old rows;
earth and stones have not been extended far.
Though it is not a place of rest,
I briefly take leisure for the long day.
There are principles for preserving life;
resting in the shade, I bid farewell to my burdens.
You, sir, illuminate my true feelings;
reaching into my heart, you grant me these scrolls of old.
At the end of autumn, I seek the distant mountains,
the mountains are far, and the journey is not short.
I part from you at the mountain bend,
filled with bitterness, I head for the long road.
In midstream, our sleeves are parted,
desiring to leave, yet my heart cannot bear it.
Looking back, my neck is not yet weary,
but at the river bend, the boat is already hidden.
The bank hides the boat, cutting off my view;
swift oars chase the rushing current.
Desiring to suppress a lifetime of joy,
I rush off on a thousand-mile journey.
At sunset, I should find a place to rest,
and tie the mooring rope by the river tower.
Not only does the evening mood withdraw,
but I remember how we stayed together.
Staying together was the joy of former times,
now adding to today's sighs.
This feeling is already divided in thought,
even more so when joined with a source of grief.
Autumn springs ring in the northern ravine,
mournful gibbons echo on the southern peaks.
Sorrowful is the heart newly parted,
deeply saddened, long-held thoughts gather!
Gathered thoughts attack the heart of parting;
at dawn, I depart from the shade of Qīngxī.
At nightfall, I seek lodging in Shànzhōng;
at dawn, I climb the peak of Tiānmǔ.
High, high it enters the clouds and rainbows;
how can the date of return be found?
If I should meet Fúqiū Gōng,
I will forever lose your fine voice.
Confined by illness, I took leave of the crowd;
leaving no trace, I entered the cloud-covered peaks.
The crags and ravines occupy my ears and eyes;
joy and love are separated from your voice and face.
Forever cutting off the hope of a kindred spirit,
long-held thoughts have no one to share them with.
At the end of the road, I met your honorable younger brother,
beaming with joy, we opened our hearts.
Once our hearts were opened,
all our shared understanding was found here.
Crossing the ravine to find my room,
opening scrolls to ask what we knew.
Evening thoughts flow with the dawn moon;
morning fears the race of the setting sun.
Conversing together without ever tiring,
but gathering and scattering become parting.
Parting, I leave Xīchuān;
the returning light goes back to Dōngshān.
Grief at the time of parting was already great;
after parting, the feelings stretch even further.
With all my thoughts, I wait for your fine news,
and indeed, I received your poem from across the river.
Diligent in the matters of wind and waves,
heartfelt are the words from the river isles.
Since you have stayed long on the isles,
the wind and waves have delayed your journey.
You strive to meet the expectations of the capital Huájīng;
how could you keep the promise of the empty valley?
Yet you still favor me with your writings,
which only serve to stir my thoughts.
If indeed you speak of returning,
let us enjoy together the late spring time.
Although late spring has not yet arrived,
mid-spring is good for roaming about.
Mountain peaches put forth red calyxes,
wild ferns gradually show purple buds.
The chirping birds are already joyful,
but my secluded dwelling is still gloomy and depressed.
In dreams, I wait for your returning boat
to release me from my regret and toil.
The Yùshuǐ records the square flow;
the Xuányuán carries the circular turn.
Storing treasures, one often lacks sound;
though secret, they are still clear and manifest.
Listening for the dragon in the Nine Springs,
hearing the phoenix, peeking into the Cinnabar Cave.
Is listening to everything truly skillful?
Only by meeting the wise men of the world.
Unfolding writings to broaden the nation's glory;
spreading words far beyond the courtly ranks.
Virtuous brilliance shines on the nation's excellence;
fragrant breezes cover the village elders.
Living like a recluse in seclusion,
the gate in the outskirts is often closed by day.
The lane in the woods sometimes opens late,
often turning back the elder's carriage.
As the courtyard darkens, I see the shadows of the wild;
as the mountains brighten, I gaze at snow on the pines.
Silently reflecting on the pervasive transformations,
this passing life enters the final season.
Pleasures past have truly ended;
when sorrow comes, it's not because joy has ceased.
Writing beautifully, I decline many letters;
with distant thoughts, I prepare this short note.
The fiery sky is now dusty and oppressive;
at the end of summer, the dust and bustle cease.
In solitary silence, I lack a companion;
facing the hall, I look at the stars.
Listening closely to the wind lashing the trees,
looking afar as the moon parts the clouds.
Night cicadas are hurried in summer;
insects in the shade are heard before autumn.
The seasons have just passed the halfway mark;
how can the fragrant herbs long remain fragrant?
Living in seclusion, I am pained by the change in things;
longing for my kind, I hold deep feelings.
The Nine Wanderings are not empty thoughts;
the Seven Weavings result in no finished pattern.
The imperial residence embodies the world's center;
its strategic defenses are but the work of Heaven.
The two palace gates block the path of carriages;
facing the forbidden area, the pure breeze is restricted.
I stand on tiptoe, staying in the Eastern Hostel,
singing in vain toward the Southern Wall.
Whether sleeping or waking, my gloom is ceaseless;
I rise to observe the stars in the Milky Way.
Floating clouds obscure the Green Gate;
the bright moon shines on the Cinnabar Palace.
Hesitating, the palace guards are strict and tight;
pacing back and forth, the water clock always runs out.
The gentleman sends fragrant news;
moved by things, my heart is pained.
I regret having no beauty from a garden hill
to emulate that tall pine.
Knowing your words have sincere consistency;
their great value is hard to match.
How can I commemorate this fine gift?
I will plant silk and paulownia.
Frail and planted, I admire upright conduct;
walking in distress, I fear losing my way first.
Rarely standing firm, not choosing a direction,
I deliberately rely on a humble dwelling.
In the past, I met with much good fortune,
holding the brush, I served the two chambers.
Although ashamed of the application of cinnabar and vermilion,
I did not think black and white would part.
Vainly I met with a time of unfairness;
the Royal Way was suddenly darkened and hazy.
Men and gods, the hidden and the manifest, were severed;
friends and loved ones were separated like clouds and rain.
Lamenting Qū at the riverbank,
seeking the Emperor on the paths of the Green Mountains.
Leaning against the rock, I listen to the lingering wind;
climbing the woods, I knot the liúyí plants.
I stand on tiptoe between the Héng and Jiào mountains;
in what month shall I look toward Qínjī?
The Imperial Sage manifests Heaven's virtue;
great benevolence raises those from the deep mud.
I regret having no transformation of the sparrow and pheasant;
how can I fill the sea and the Huái?
Leaving the capital to return to my old village,
at my secluded gate, I plant mugwort and goosefoot.
Gathering thorns to thatch my old house,
cutting away briars to open the old fields.
Things decline as the time grows late;
the years pass, but my ambitions do not keep pace.
Being close to the virtuous, I spread my affection;
inspired to write poems, I investigate literary dwelling.
The fragrance rests in the orchids;
the clear sound surpasses fine jade.
Exhausting my words, this is not just a response;
I use it only to express what is in my heart.
Chángqīng was the crown of Huáyáng;
Zhònglián excelled in Hǎiyīn.
Jade vessels are indeed a treasury of literature;
profound principles are also the heart of the Way.
The gentleman raises his high carriage;
the dusty tracks indeed form a forest.
Noble feelings match distant traces;
pure qi overflows the simple lapel.
Our friendship ignores the difference in age;
devoted care discards the ups and downs of fortune.
In the cold of winter, we rest and sun ourselves together;
with spring wine, we occasionally pour for each other.
Recently the year has turned warm;
light clouds emerge from the eastern peak.
The wheat ridges have much beautiful color;
the willow garden flows with fine sounds.
I enjoy this leisure of the day,
suddenly forgetting the intrusion of the passing light.
With what can I comfort my hidden heart?
With brush and ink, I have long chanted and sung.
The perching phoenix finds it hard to find a branch;
your kind gift is not what I expected.
I chant it to keep it with me forever,
I case it in a box as if it were worth twice its weight in gold.
The structure is so lofty and distant,
Gazing out, it reaches the extremes of height and depth.
Within the windows are lined distant peaks,
At the edge of the courtyard, I look down upon tall forests.
As the sun rises, the many birds disperse,
As the mountains darken, a lone gibbon cries.
Already there is wine upon the pond,
And again, this zither in the wind.
Were it not for your boundless beauty,
Who would trouble my small heart?
You are kind and able to favor me,
Asking after me with the sound of Yáohuá.
If you leave your steps at the Jīnmén,
Come seek me at the peaks of Yùshān.
Like the "legs and arms" governor of Huáiyáng,
You still lie high and reclined here.
Moreover, in the bend of Nánshān,
How is it different from a time of secluded dwelling?
Continuous overcast skies mark the peak of the farming season,
Bamboo hats and rain capes gather in the eastern fields.
The high pavilion is often closed during the day,
The wild steps have few voices of contention.
Fine mats cool the summer room,
Light fans stir a chilly breeze.
Fine bream can briefly be presented,
Clear "green ant" wine is held alone.
Summer plums submerge their red fruit,
Autumn lotus roots break into light silk threads.
Where after all is the auspicious time?
Formerly I dreamed of a fine meeting.
Sitting and whistling is merely cumulative,
A full year has passed in governing the state.
In the end, I cannot take to the music of strings and songs,
Leaning on the desk makes me laugh at myself.
The Dà Jiāng flows day and night,
The traveler's heart's sorrow is without end.
I only think of how close the mountain passes are,
Yet finally know the return path is long.
The Autumn River glimmers at dawn,
The cold islet is dark and vast at night.
Turning my head, I see the capital's chambers,
The palace walls are just now in view.
Golden waves beautify the Zhīquè pavilion,
The Jade Rope hangs low over the Jiànzhāng palace.
Driving my carriage outside the Dǐngmén,
I long to see the sunny side of Zhāoqiū.
The racing sunlight cannot be caught,
How much more so when separated by two regions.
Wind and clouds have paths for birds,
The Jiāng and Hàn rivers are limited by a lack of bridges.
Constantly I fear the strike of hawks and falcons,
Or that the seasonal chrysanthemums will wither in the harsh frost.
I send word to those with nets and traps:
In the vast emptiness, I have already soared high.
Rustling, the branches grow strong early,
Thick and muddy, the dew dries late.
In the south, the oranges and pomelos flourish,
How would they know of the wild geese flying?
Brushing away the mist, I head to the Blue Pavilion in the morning,
Until the sun is late, I sit in the Red Portal.
Disappointed, I gaze at the one blocked path,
A hundred uneven worries depend on it.
Spring grass turns even greener in autumn,
Yet the young lord has not returned west.
Who can stay long in Jīngluò?
The black dust stains one's plain white clothes.
Receiving fine favor, I serve the Emperor's son,
Stepping in my shoes, I attend the Prince.
It happened that I was favored with a post in the Jīnmǎ Bureau,
And again graced the Tónglóng Gate.
I go in and out of the Píngjīn residence,
Once seeing the goblet of Mèng Cháng.
Returning home, I am shaded by mulberries and elms,
Morning and evening, the cool and warm are different.
Withering and falling is indeed said to be so,
Silence and insignificance remain thus from start to finish.
Closing the door to clear the "three paths,"
I sit by the railing overlooking the winding pond.
Wild ducks and cranes call to their companions,
Lotus and water chestnuts begin to grow unevenly.
Though there are no "tian tian" leaves,
I drift upon the ripples with you.
Spring flowers and autumn fruits,
Sons of concubines and household ministers.
Why the princely gates are honored,
Is that since ancient times they have many talented people.
The detached palaces gather "cedar and cypress,"
The grand houses are rich with men like Xú and Chén.
At dawn, in the Shànglín Park,
At sunset, by the banks of the Yī River.
The secretaries are already elegant and swift,
Their rhapsodies and songs can be exquisitely peerless.
Xiāngrú would be ashamed of their warmth and beauty,
Zǐyún would be embarrassed by their calligraphy and writing.
Swift steeds long for the long slope,
Brushwood carts fear the dangerous ruts.
I am ashamed of this Shānyáng banquet,
In vain is this Héyáng parting.
Drinking for ten days on the Píngyuán,
The Zhōngsàn travels a thousand miles.
Bóhǎi is just now flooded and stagnant,
Who in Yíchéng will offer a toast?
Living in seclusion under Nánshān,
Facing this season as autumn begins.
Alas, the time is not with me,
As the sun sets, there is no light boat.
The farming families go out to gather wood,
And only return as dusk falls.
I then hear my young child say,
That a guest knocked at the brushwood gate.
The attendants were all adorned with pearls and tortoiseshell,
Their furs and horses were all light and fat.
Their carriages and canopies illuminated the village,
Their official tallies brought forth a radiant glow.
I suspected it was the Governor of Xúfāng,
Yet having suspected it, I doubted it again.
That people "remember old friends" was said in the past,
But this way has become slight today.
The worldly mind rejects the flawed and lowly,
Why would you alone look upon my humble gate?
I regret not having prepared the chicken and millet,
To be able to share them with my old friend.
My heart is filled with feelings in vain,
My tears fall fruitlessly in profusion.
I send this letter to the geese among the clouds,
To fly toward the northwest for me.
Acting in office at the Qīngsuǒ Gate,
I gaze from afar at the Fènghuáng Pool.
Who says the distance between us is great?
Yet silently, your luminous presence is blocked.
Mount Dài is rich in spiritual wonders,
The Yí River is abundant in heroic talents.
Extraordinary wings soar over the Běihǎi,
Spiraling up to depart from Nánpí.
Having encountered a sagely and enlightened sovereign,
You come to roost upon the branches of the firmiana tree.
How lush are the bamboo flowers,
How numerous are the firmiana leaves!
One can roost and one can eat,
Beyond this, what else is there to do?
How could it be like the wren,
For whom a single grain is more than enough?
Setting out in the morning from Fùchūn Islet,
I harbor my thoughts and endure the longing.
The Magistrate of Zhuó returns from his spring rounds,
Carriages and canopies overflow the riverbanks.
Having gazed for long, we finally gather,
Sorrow and joy cannot be restrained.
The road along the Cāngjiāng ends here,
The rapids and dangers begin from this point.
Layered peaks easily create echoes,
Redoubled by the sorrow of gibbons at night.
A traveler's heart might fortunately be calmed,
But midway I meet the one I longed for.
Close friends are separated from this point on,
And I take my leave from here for a solitary journey.
My humble person is as light as a cicada’s wing,
At twenty, I was unworthy of the gracious invitation.
During mourning, I obstructed the path of the worthy,
Twice I ascended to the court of the Prime Minister.
Humbly I received the recommendation of Gōngshū,
Successively I served in the Prince’s office.
With a long whistle, I returned to Dōngshān,
Clasping a plow to weed the seasonal sprouts.
In the secluded valley, fine kudzu grows lushly,
On the steep cliffs, flowering branches spread.
Fallen petals drop at the foot of the woods,
Flying stems stand tall above the hills.
Low and high—what is constant?
Rise and fall happen in a single morning.
I only regret that during these prosperous times,
The way of the petty man has finally dwindled.
Like a tumbleweed in a wild field,
Whirling and drifting with the wind.
Once weary of traveling the capital,
Now I manage the labor service in Héshuò.
Climbing the wall, I look longingly toward the south,
The gentle wind stirs my fine silk.
The great current of the Hé River is vast,
The long mountains are lush and towering.
Who says the Jìn capital is far?
The house is near, but my person is truly distant.
Who says a district magistrate's post is light?
I fear only that my good reputation is not excellent.
Life between heaven and earth—
Who can guarantee a hundred years?
Brilliant as a spark from a flint,
Fleeting as a whirlwind crossing the path.
In the capital of Qí, no songs were left behind,
In Tóngxiāng, there are lingering folk songs.
Blessings for the humble lie in pure simplicity,
Harm for the full comes from pride and arrogance.
Although I lack the virtue to rule over people,
I look upon the commoners and hope not to be frivolous.
At sunset, dark clouds arise,
Climbing the wall to gaze at the great Hé River.
River mists shroud the mountain ridges,
Startling rapids dash against the rocky bends.
Returning geese are reflected in the orchid fields,
Swimming fish stir circular ripples.
Chirping cicadas raise their shrill cold notes,
Seasonal chrysanthemums shine with autumn blossoms.
Stretching my neck to gaze at the capital city,
The southern road lies in the cutting of the axe handle.
Dàxià is remote and cannot be seen,
The lofty mountains are lush and jagged.
The bustling people of the capital city,
Their customs are in turmoil and corrupted.
Following the water like floating duckweed,
Clinging to pines like hanging vines.
Zhū Bó corrected laxness and laziness,
The customs of Chǔ covered Lángyá.
How can a crooked tumbleweed be straightened?
By leaning its body against a cluster of hemp.
What is constant for the common people?
Success in governance lies in the harmony of the people.
My position is the same as in Shānfù district,
I am ashamed to lack the song of Zǐjiàn.
How could I dare despise a humble office?
I only fear being unworthy of what I bear.
The southern path welcomes the long daylight,
The summer god sends off the final rays.
The first heat begins the new season,
The intense heat is just now blazing.
In the morning, I think of auspicious clouds rising,
In the evening, I wait for the bright sun to move.
Wiping sweat, I leave the central hall,
